context:
Goal: browser rules that make the build better, with no load nobody needs.
Problem (rule): the new browser rules (PR #962) say a repo that names no browsers must use only web features that every major browser has supported for about two and a half years (the web's "Baseline Widely available" list). That is a standard level set by default, and your 12:23 CST ruling says no standard level is taken on by choice.
Based on (read): the round 3 reviewer of PR #962 flagged it as a note; your ruling of Nov 1 12:23 CST.
Departs from: main (no browser-support rule) — adds a default: features every major browser has had for about two and a half years.

Not blocking: #962 is in the batch with option a, and the rule works as written until you pick.

options.gain: Pages work in the browsers people actually have, with no setup per repo.
options.how: A repo that names no browsers uses features on the Baseline Widely available list.
options.label: Keep the default: features all major browsers have had for a while
options.lose: A repo that wants a newer feature adds a fallback or names its own browsers.

options.how: The rule checks nothing until a repo writes one line naming its browsers.
options.label: No default: each web repo names its own browsers
options.lose: Each repo needs that line once; until then, nothing is checked.

options.how: Remove the browser-support rule from the house rules.
options.label: Drop the rule
options.lose: A new web feature can ship broken in some browsers with no check.

reply: Kept: the rule shipped with a in batch 56 (#965).
title: Which browsers should a web page work in when its repo names none?
why: It is the browsers people really use, not an extra standard: a page that breaks in them is a worse build.
